thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: SEV2 - serving-cluster-a reports elevated InfiniBand retransmits (>10%) and multiple container restarts. Symptoms: latency spikes, 503s for heavy-embedding routes. Pager: @mira.sre. thread_ts=1793506789

mira.sre: Ack, I'm oncall and investigating. First pass: which nodes?

zane.eng-runtime: I'm seeing GPU container crashes with `CUDA error: unspecified launch failure` around the same time as IB timeouts. Correlation looks strong.

mira.sre: @nate.infra can you pull IB fabric health and switch counters for rack-a?

nate.infra: fetching counters now. Running `perfquery -x` and `ibstat` on the affected leafs.

nate.infra: paste: ```
# ibstat node-310
CA 'mlx5_0'
  state: Active
  phys_state: LinkUp
# mlx5_qp 0 stats:
  retransmissions: 1284
  rx_packets: 543210
  tx_packets: 538900
  rx_errors: 102
  1min_retransmit_pct: 12.3%
```

mira.sre: Ugh. retransmit spike >=12%. That explains the KV cache misses and repeated retries triggering OOMs.

zane.eng-runtime: Logs from serving pod on node-310: ```
[2026-03-08T03:12:21Z] WARN network: rdma timeout seq=412
[2026-03-08T03:12:23Z] ERROR runtime: KVCache miss and full batching spike
[2026-03-08T03:12:24Z] FATAL cuda: cuCtxCreate failed: out of memory
```

linh.prodops: Quick customer impact note: Embedding-heavy customers A and C saw ~30% increase in error rates starting 03:12 UTC. Routing currently still to cluster-a by default.

mira.sre: Mitigation plan 1 (immediate): enable TCP fallback routing for heavy routes, drain problematic nodes, and route new traffic to cluster-b. Mitigation plan 2 (short): remove flapping NICs or take node offline for firmware reload.

nate.infra: Initiating node drain for node-310 and node-312. Command: `kubectl drain node-310 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (rolling will avoid global outage).

deploy-bot: Canary reroute job started: `routing/shift` 20% -> cluster-b for model embeddings-large.

customer-ops: Notifying impacted customers (A,C). Sending interim support message: "We're aware of increased errors for embeddings, routing to an alternate cluster; engineering is investigating."

zane.eng-runtime: Meanwhile I can enable the runtime fallback to gRPC/TCP for new sessions: `redwoodctl set-routing --service embeddings-large --fallback tcp` This will preserve correctness at cost of increased latency. Proceed?

mira.sre: Do it. Prioritize preserving customer success over p99 latency. Execute and monitor effects.

zane.eng-runtime: Done. `redwoodctl` output: ```
Applied fallback tcp for embeddings-large
Affected nodes: cluster-a pool-3
Traffic shift: new sessions will prefer tcp until fab healthy
```

nate.infra: After draining node-310/312, retransmits dropped from 12% -> 3% on remaining leafs. We're seeing less queueing. However two NICs report firmware flaps. Opening ticket with vendor for firmware push.

mira.sre: @linh.prodops please confirm customer errors falling.

linh.prodops: Partial: error rate for A and C down ~60% since routing change and drains. Latency increased ~150ms p95 but acceptable for now.

customer-ops: Customers acknowledge and are in maintenance window for some. One enterprise customer requests SLA credit assessment. Capturing impacts.

zane.eng-runtime: Warning: some legacy clients still hold long-lived KV sessions on affected nodes and we observed a couple of `container restart` loops. I'm initiating a rolling restart of serving pods on drained nodes only. Command snippet: ```
kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-pool-3 --namespace=prod --field-selector=spec.nodeName=node-312
```

nate.infra: While restarts run, we toggled link-level logging to DEBUG and temporarily increased RDMA MTT and timeouts. Commands applied at switch level: `set mtu 4096; set ib_timeout 60`.

mira.sre: Good. Any sign of CUDA OOMs after drain and tcp fallback?

zane.eng-runtime: No new CUDA OOM stack traces after traffic shifted and restarts finished. A few older pods still show repeated restarts in system logs but they're now isolated.

linh.prodops: Prepare Handoff: I'm going to hand this to night oncall in 10m. Current state: fabric counters improved to 2-4% retransmit, customer error rates reduced to baseline+5-10%, fallback to TCP active for embeddings-large, two nodes out of rotation pending firmware update. Action items for night: vendor firmware, complete post-incident storage of logs, draft postmortem, and check routing revert test.

mira.sre: Acknowledged. @zane can you take oncall for the next 2 hours? I'll remain available for escalations.

zane.eng-runtime: I can take it. I'll keep monitoring and leave runbook notes in #incidents-handovers.

deploy-bot: Routing canary increased to 60% -> cluster-b per scheduled ramp. Monitor for anomalies.

nate.infra: Ticket to vendor: INC-2241 created with NIC vendor, severity high, attached logs and `ibdiagnet` dumps. ETA firmware push 12-24h depending on vendor window.

mira.sre: Thanks team. Summary for post-incident: root suspected flapping NICs causing IB packet loss -> increased retransmits -> request stalls -> KV cache pressure -> GPU memory blowouts and container restarts. Immediate mitigations: drain bad nodes, enabled TCP fallback, rerouted traffic to cluster-b, rolling restarts. Next steps: vendor firmware, improve automatic fallback detection thresholds, add quicker routing playbook to switch to fallback sooner, customer SLA write-up.

linh.prodops: I'm sending the incident notification now and will start the postmortem doc template. Link to follow in this thread. :white_check_mark:

customer-ops: We'll follow up with customers and coordinate SLA.

mira.sre: Handing over fully to @zane.eng-runtime at 1793508599. If anything spikes, page me. Closing active paging for this incident and will create postmortem.

oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged closed to paging at 1793508599. Postmortem: https://redwood.internal/incident/1793506789/postmortem (draft) "IB fabric packetloss -> serving node flaps"

zane.eng-runtime: Logged runbook notes and open action items. I'll follow up in AM with vendor outcome. Good job everyone. :pray:
